blocks.why: Full night in your own bed before the first all-nighter of the month.
Bank a nap before the GRU night sector; up 1h20 before I leave at 15:05Z so I'm clear of the fog for the drive.
Straight down at the hotel after the 02:10 local landing, while sleep pressure is still doing the work.
Top-up before another 13h40 all-nighter home; awake an hour before the 19:35Z pickup.
Home at 10:35Z off a night flight — three hours to take the edge off, then stop so I can still sleep tonight.
Proper night at home to reset before the ORD trip.
Pre-duty nap for the westbound; done two hours before I leave at 15:05Z.
22:30-06:00 Chicago time — lands on the local night and my body night both, so take the whole thing.
Second Chicago night, up nearly two hours before the 13:20Z pickup for the 08:45 local report.
In the door at 01:10Z and straight to bed — this is the main sleep, not a nap.
Two hours before the 22:10Z departure to ORD; finished 1h45 before I leave at 19:45Z.
Hotel at 02:35 local off the night flight — sleep now while the pressure is high.
Second sleep on Chicago nights before the day sector home.
Home 01:10Z after the last ORD leg — eight hours, no alarm needed.
Anchor night to pull me back onto London time before standby.
Normal night — on standby you want to be fully rested from midday in case the phone goes.
Standard night at home on a day off.
Early to bed for the 08:00 local sim; up at 05:00Z to leave at 06:05Z.
Back to a normal night after the sim.
Days off — keep the same times so the body clock stays put.
Days off — hold the routine.
Days off — hold the routine.
Days off — hold the routine.
Days off — hold the routine.
Last full night before the GRU trip; plenty of margin for the 09:15Z departure from home.
Hotel at 21:15 local after a 13h40 duty — that's 01:45 body time, so it's a real night's sleep.
18:00-20:00 local is 22:00-midnight body time, so this nap will actually happen; capped at two hours and done 1h15 before the 00:15Z pickup.
Home at 15:15Z off an all-night sector — two hours only, so tonight still works.
Recovery night after the GRU return; this is where the debt gets paid back.
Second recovery night at home.
Eight hours before the LAX day sector; up at 05:30Z with time to spare on the 06:50Z departure from home.
15:30 local looks odd but it's midnight to 07:30 on my clock — I'm only here two nights so I'm staying on London time.
Mid-afternoon by body time — a short one to bridge a long day off in LA.
Main sleep sitting on my body night again, held as late as I can so I'm not up for hours before report.
Two hours before the flight home — the back end of that sector is deep in the small hours body time, so I want this.
Home at 05:40Z off the redeye; three hours, then up and out in the daylight so I can go down early tonight.
Early bed for a 06:00 local standby report — sleep before an early start is the sleep you never get, so start it early.
Closing the month out with a normal night after the standby.

conflicts.statement: PW899 LHR-GRU is planned report 16:00Z to release 05:40Z+1 — 13h40 of flight duty against the FCM §4.1.3 ceiling of 13h.
options: Ask crewing which basis this FDP was built on — if it's an augmented crew with onboard rest, get that stated on the pairing so you know before you sign for it
If it isn't augmented, raise it with the operator now rather than on the day; 40 minutes over a hard ceiling is their call to fix, not yours to absorb
Either way, take the 12:00-13:45Z nap — this duty ends at 06:40 local having flown right through the small hours

conflicts.statement: PW700 GRU-LHR is report 20:00Z to release 09:40Z+1 — 13h40, again over the 13h planning ceiling, and it is the second 13h40 all-nighter in a row.
options: Raise this with the same query as 09-01; it's one pairing and should be answered once
Protect the 06:30-14:00Z sleep in GRU — if the hotel room is noisy or bright, ask for a change on arrival rather than losing it
If you land at LHR feeling worse than the plan assumes, file a fatigue report; the two 13h40 nights back to back are the reason

conflicts.statement: PW135 LHR-GRU is report 10:10Z to release 23:50Z — 13h40, over the FCM §4.1.3 ceiling.
options: Same query to crewing as the September 1-2 pairing; both GRU rotations are built the same way
You start this one well rested off six days off, which is the best position you'll be in for it

conflicts.statement: PW344 GRU-LHR is report 00:40Z to release 14:20Z — 13h40, over the ceiling, and the whole duty runs through the body-clock night.
options: Include this leg in the crewing query about the two GRU pairings
This is the duty on the roster I would least want to be short of sleep for — see the 09-23 sleep conflict below

conflicts.statement: The 09-22 roster line prints report 00:40Z+1 with STD/STA/off-duty all marked +1 as well, so it is unclear whether the duty runs on 09-22 or 09-23. Read against the row date it falls on 09-23, giving a 24h50 GRU layover, and that is what I have planned. The other reading puts report at 00:40Z on 09-22 — 50 minutes after the previous release at 23:50Z on 09-21 — which would breach the 10-hour rest minimum outright. I have also therefore treated 09-22 as the layover day and 09-23 as the duty day, which is the reverse of how the roster marks them.
options: Get crewing to confirm the report date in writing before 09-21 — this is a one-line answer from them and the whole GRU pairing hangs on it
If it does turn out to be 00:40Z on 09-22, that is a 50-minute rest period: you cannot report, and 117.25 puts the notification on you
If the confirmed answer is 09-23, the plan below stands unchanged

conflicts.statement: In the 24 hours ending when PW344 lands at 13:50Z you will have had about 2 hours of sleep — the 2-hour evening nap and nothing else. You wake at 08:15Z on 09-22 and are then awake, apart from that nap, until release at 14:20Z on 09-23: roughly 30 hours across a 13h40 duty that flies straight through the window of circadian low. This is the sharpest fatigue exposure in the month and it comes from a 23:10 local departure after a full layover day; no arrangement of the layover fixes it completely.
options: Extend the evening block to a split sleep of about 5 hours, roughly 17:00-22:00Z (14:00-19:00 local), instead of the 2-hour nap — it breaks nap-cap-2h and you may only get part of it, but hours in the bank beat a clean rule here
Keep the 2-hour nap as planned and instead agree the in-flight rest order with the crew before departure so you get the first break, closest to the body-clock low
Ask crewing for a later report or a second night in GRU on this pairing
Plan nothing for the afternoon of 09-23 beyond the recovery nap — no drive further than home, and let someone else collect you if that is an option

conflicts.statement: In the 24 hours ending at release from PW353 at 04:45Z you get about 3h45 — the tail of the LAX main sleep plus the 2-hour pre-duty nap. The last four hours of that sector sit between 01:00 and 05:00 body time.
options: Take the full 12:00-14:00Z nap in LAX even if you don't feel like it; it is the only sleep inside the duty window you can plan for
Take the earlier in-flight rest slot if the crew complement allows one
Do not drive yourself home off this one if you can avoid it — the 05:40Z arrival home is 22:40 body time on the LA clock and you'll have been up a long time
The 06:00-09:00Z recovery nap on 09-29 is deliberately capped at three hours so the 19:30Z bedtime still works ahead of the 06:00 local standby

conflicts.statement: Across the 24 hours spanning the overnight GRU-LHR sector you land about 4h30 of sleep against your 7h30 target — 1h30 of pre-duty nap plus the 3-hour recovery nap after you get home at 10:35Z. This is inherent to a night flight home and the plan pays it back with 8 hours the following night.
options: Extend the 09-03 recovery nap to about 5 hours if you're struggling, accepting that the following night will be broken
Keep it at three hours as planned and get outside in daylight in the afternoon — it's the faster route back onto London time before 09-04
You have 30h20 before the next report, so there is no rest-period pressure here; this is purely about how you choose to spend it
